reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION LOWER-CASE of an alphabetic or alphanumeric argument (an alphanumeric or alphabetic elementary item, an alphanumeric-edited item, a group, a reference-modified item or a nonnumeric literal) returns the same character string with each uppercase letter replaced by its lowercase letter and every other character unchanged.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window sig.IntroducedIn (85): LOWER-CASE admitted at 85
Constructs.CaseFunctionLocalePhrase2014: the LOCALE phrase is refused below 2014

the CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION arm (ctx.Data.Configuration.Classification), reachable only from a 2002 OBJECT-COMPUTER clause; at 85 the plain invariant arm is taken, the arm 2023 takes without a classification

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs and CobolIntrinsics.Text.cs for Edition, DialectLevel, DialectBehavior, ConstructRegistry; the runtime LowerCase body has no edition input.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf38_06 covers PIC X, PIC A and a literal with mixed case, digits and punctuation; it does not cover a group, an edited item, a reference-modified or ODO argument, characters next to the letter range, letters outside A-Z, or an argument that is also the receiver.

reader.notes: The runtime maps the argument's image with ToLowerInvariant, which lowers exactly the letters that have a lowercase form and leaves every other character, so the string and its length are kept. COBOL1627's text at 85 lists national classes and cites §2023 only; that is a wording matter for the argument rule (A.2.22.3 AR1), not this returned-value rule.

refuter.evidence: Argument class alphanumeric in 1985 includes numeric-edited items (class alphanumeric), which the reader's requirement omitted; probe rlc1.cob at --std 85 (runs/rlc1-001): ZZ9.99CR with -12.5 -> ' 12.50cr' length 8, ZZ9.99DB -> '  3.00db'; PIC A(6) 'AB CD ' -> 'ab cd '; JUSTIFIED RIGHT -> '    xy'; 66 RENAMES -> 'abcd'; reference-modified R2B(2:) -> 'fghij'.
